venue: Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium, Lafayette, La.

preview.headline: USA's run game against a rested Louisiana defense, with the West on the line.
preview.summary: Both teams are 2-2 in the Sun Belt, two games behind unbeaten Louisiana Tech. South Alabama has lost three of four and was shut out in the second half last week; Louisiana is coming off a bye after a 35-31 loss at Southern Miss.

matchup.why: USA scores more, but managed 13 at Marshall and 20 against Louisiana Tech in its last two games.
The biggest gap on the page. Louisiana's red-zone offense scores on 96.7% of trips (4th); USA's red-zone defense allows scores on 85.7%.
USA allows 402.1 yards a game (113th); Louisiana allows 317.3 (31st).

matchup.metric: USA run game vs. Louisiana run defense
matchup.why: USA's best weapon. Southern Miss ran 43 times for 286 yards (6.7 a carry) against Louisiana on Oct. 24.

matchup.metric: Louisiana run game vs. USA run defense
matchup.why: QB Lunch Winfield has 9 rushing TDs. Louisiana's offense runs first; its passing game ranks 107th.
Close. USA lost the turnover battle 2-0 against Louisiana Tech, including a fumble at its own 6.
USA was flagged 12 times for 100 yards against Louisiana Tech. That is hard to overcome on the road.

usa: Run the ball the way Southern Miss did. Louisiana allowed 286 rushing yards in its last game; USA averages 213.1 and ran for 205 against Louisiana Tech.
Cut the penalties. 12 flags for 100 yards last week against a Louisiana team that averages 43.4 penalty yards, 20th in FBS.
Finish drives after halftime. USA had 397 yards but 0 second-half points against Tech and went 1 of 4 on fourth down.
opp: Win in the red zone. Louisiana scores on 96.7% of red-zone trips and USA's defense allows scores on 85.7%.
Control the clock with the run. Louisiana holds the ball 33:33 a game (6th in FBS) and is fresh off a bye; long drives keep USA's offense on the sideline.

players.name: Keenan Phillips
players.note: 107 carries, 576 yards, 6 TD. Had 11 carries for 62 yards and a lost fumble against Tech while PJ Martin ran 12 times for 82; watch how the carries split.

players.name: Jared Hollins
players.note: 82-of-156 (52.6%), 1,195 yards, 9 TD, 4 INT. Under 50% in each of the last two games (12-of-33, then 14-of-31); Louisiana allows 5.9 yards a pass.

players.name: Lunch Winfield
players.note: 130-of-195, 1,452 yards, 6 TD, 5 INT, plus 470 rushing yards and 9 rushing TD. Threw for 299 at Southern Miss but was 22-of-41 and ran 13 times for 7 yards.

players.name: Jake St. Andre
players.note: Louisiana's leading tackler with 60. Had 11 tackles, a sack and a forced fumble at Southern Miss; the player USA's line has to reach on run plays.

watch.title: Anthony Eager vs. Louisiana's secondary
watch.text: Eager caught 7 passes for 102 yards and both USA touchdown passes against Tech. Louisiana's pass defense allows 190.3 yards a game (38th).

watch.title: Rest vs. rhythm
watch.text: Louisiana had the Oct. 31 bye; USA plays for the third straight week after Marshall (Oct. 20) and Louisiana Tech (Oct. 31). Watch the fourth quarter.

watch.title: The West race
watch.text: Louisiana Tech is 4-0 in the league with five teams at 2-2, including both of these. The loser drops two games back with three left.

injuries: No injury report found for either team as of Nov. 5 (checked ESPN, FOX10, BVM Sports, 103.3 The GOAT).
Keenan Phillips' lighter workload against Tech (11 carries) was not explained in any source found.
preview.weather: ESPN/AccuWeather forecast for kickoff (checked Nov. 5): 72°F, 0% chance of rain, gusts to 15 mph. Artificial turf.

lastGame.usa: Lost 35-20 to Louisiana Tech at home on Oct. 31 (shut out in the second half, 12 penalties for 100 yards, 2 turnovers).
lastGame.opp: Lost 35-31 at Southern Miss on Oct. 24 (allowed 286 rushing yards), then had a bye on Oct. 31.

prediction.reasoning: Louisiana's defense allows 1.6 yards a play less than USA's, it is at home, rested, and nearly automatic in the red zone. USA's run game is good enough to exploit the same holes Southern Miss found, which keeps it within one score.
prediction.risks: If USA runs for 250-plus and stays out of the penalty column, the Jaguars can win, as they did on their last two trips to Lafayette. Winfield's passing has been inconsistent (5 INT, 22-of-41 last game), so USA turnovers could flip the margin.

preview.context: Louisiana leads the all-time series 10-4 and won 31-22 in Mobile last season (Nov. 1, 2025). USA won its last two games in Lafayette, including 20-17 on a last-second field goal in 2022. Louisiana's three losses: at USC (49-30), at Louisiana Tech (32-31) and at Southern Miss (35-31); it is 4-0 at home. Kickoff 4 p.m. Central on ESPN+ and the Jags Radio Network.

grade.summary: The brief picked Louisiana 30-24 and Louisiana won 28-26, so the winner was right, the margin was off by 4 and the total (54) was exact. It was right that Louisiana's run game would control the game, but USA's own run game did not break out, and the brief never saw Bishop Davenport starting at quarterback in place of Jared Hollins.

keys.key: USA: Run the ball the way Southern Miss did.
keys.note: 35 carries for 159 yards (4.5 a carry), well short of USA's 213.1 average and Southern Miss' 286. Keenan Phillips had 9 carries for 19 yards; Davenport's 45-yard TD run was the only big gain.
9 for 65 yards, down from 12 for 100 against Tech and close to Louisiana's 10 for 60. Penalties did not decide this one.
9 second-half points (45-yard TD run, 50-yard FG) but a failed two-point try at 23-28 and Davenport's interception at the Louisiana 35 with under two minutes left ended the last drive.

keys.key: Louisiana: Win in the red zone.
keys.note: Louisiana scored on its one red-zone trip (Winfield 14-yard run), but its other TDs came from outside it: a 100-yard kickoff return, a 65-yard run and a 27-yard pass. Big plays, not the red zone, decided it.

keys.key: Louisiana: Control the clock with the run.
keys.note: 44 carries for 312 yards (7.1 a carry), 31:37 time of possession and 8 of 13 on third down; an 11-play, 6:20 drive in the fourth quarter ran clock before a missed FG.

players.name: Keenan Phillips
players.note: 9 carries, 19 yards (2.1 a carry), 1 catch for 7; fumbled twice, lost neither. Carries split four ways with Davenport (11-57), Trae'von Dunbar (7-47) and PJ Martin (7-37).

players.name: Jared Hollins
players.note: Did not record a stat. Bishop Davenport played quarterback: 16 of 22, 210 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT, plus 11 carries for 57 yards and 2 TD. No source found explaining the change.

players.name: Lunch Winfield
players.note: 10 of 14, 147 yards, 1 TD (27 yards to Shelton Sampson Jr.), 1 INT returned 72 yards for a USA TD by Jaylen Moson; 19 carries, 97 yards, 1 TD.

players.name: Jake St. Andre
players.note: Led Louisiana with 9 tackles, 1 sack and 1 tackle for loss.

grade.missed: It did not flag JJ Garner, who returned the opening kickoff 100 yards for a TD and ran 10 times for 136 yards, including a 65-yard TD. It assumed Hollins would start; Davenport played the whole game. Brendan Jenkins (6 catches, 101 yards) was USA's top receiver, not Anthony Eager (3 for 38), and USA's defensive TD and two Dylan Freebury field goals (44 and 50) kept a game close that Louisiana outgained 459 to 369.

performance.summary: A two-point road loss to a 6-3 Louisiana team that is unbeaten at home. USA averaged 6.5 yards a play (369 on 57), got a 72-yard pick-six and two long field goals, and Davenport was efficient (16 of 22, 210 yards). But the defense allowed 312 rushing yards at 7.1 a carry and 8 of 13 on third down, kick coverage gave up a 100-yard TD on the first play, the offense was 4 of 12 on third down, and the final drive ended in an interception.

accuracy.note: Picked Louisiana by 6; Louisiana won by 2, off by 4.
Picked 54 points; the game had 54, off by 0.
2 of 5 keys held up: USA cut its penalties and Louisiana controlled the game on the ground.
Winfield, St. Andre and the Phillips carry split mattered, and the loser did fall two games back in the West; Hollins did not play and Garner, the game's best player, was not mentioned.

fixes.title: Run defense
fixes.text: 312 rushing yards at 7.1 a carry, including Garner's 65-yard TD and Winfield's 97 yards. Troy comes to Mobile on Nov 14; USA cannot let another opponent run at will.

fixes.title: Kickoff coverage
fixes.text: Garner took the opening kickoff 100 yards for a TD. That was 7 points in a 2-point loss before USA's defense took the field.

fixes.title: Third downs on both sides
fixes.text: USA converted 4 of 12; Louisiana converted 8 of 13. Louisiana held the ball 31:37 largely by staying on schedule.

fixes.title: Late-game execution
fixes.text: A failed two-point run at 23-28 and an interception at the Louisiana 35 with under two minutes left, down 2, ended USA's last two chances.

fixes.title: Get the backs going
fixes.text: Phillips, Martin and Dunbar combined for 23 carries and 103 yards; the run game was 54 yards a game below its average. Find a lead back against Troy.
